Why does the model look the wrong size?
STL files do not store units. Use Load → Advanced to set source units or scale. All working dimensions are in millimetres. Confirm a known dimension before splitting.
The whole model is striped. Did the split fail?
The Fit/Model view shows the unsplit model in its current pose. The split result reports whether each piece fits in its chosen print orientation. Those are separate checks.
Why is a joint different from the style I chose?
The face may be too thin or shallow. Read the substitution warning. Select that contact to choose a seam, a keyed connection, a forced attempt, or a return to automatic placement.
Can I save and reopen the editing session?

Printer and preference settings persist locally. The loaded mesh, cut tree and joint edits do not persist across reloads. Keep your source file and download the completed package before closing the page.

**Split a 3D model that is too big for your printer into parts that fit, with joints on every cut face, and export print-ready plates and an assembly sheet.**
**Live:** <https://magnusp.is/splitter/>. It runs entirely in your browser. Your model is never uploaded.

1. **Load** an STL (binary or ASCII), OBJ or 3MF up to 300 MB. The mesh is welded and repaired: holes are capped, flipped and inside-out faces are fixed, duplicate and degenerate faces are removed, non-manifold edges are split and debris is dropped. Each repair is counted in the UI. Meshes above 600k triangles are simplified for planning (closed shells kept, measured deviation shown) and parts are
2. **Choose a printer** (Prusa, Bambu Lab, Creality, Voron presets, or a custom volume) and a safety margin.

3. **Auto split.** A BSP search over cut planes trades part count against estimated support demand. The **Fewer parts ↔ Less support** slider defaults to Balanced; move it fully left for the legacy parts-first objective. You can move, tilt, delete or add cuts. **Auto-complete** then splits only the parts that still do not fit.

4. **Joints.** Every cut face is analysed, and joints are placed where the wall can hold them. You can edit them on a 2D joint map, which opens as a large zoomable editor (wheel/pinch, keyboard, phone layout) with the 3D view optionally beside it.
5. **Build** every part as a closed manifold solid with the [Manifold](https://github.com/elalish/manifold) kernel. The interference between mating parts is checked.
6. **Export** a zip: oriented STLs, one 3MF per print plate, an all-plates 3MF, an assembled preview, an HTML assembly sheet, `plan.json` and a per-part report.

- Each cut face is rasterised and split into **contact patches**, one for each pair of parts that touch there.
- A Euclidean distance transform of each patch gives the largest inscribed circle at every point. Its ridge is the medial axis, and the typical ridge value gives the wall thickness.

- A point joint may sit only where the distance is at least joint radius + clearance + minimum wall. The minimum wall is 2 × nozzle × 1.05 and never below 1.2 mm. This stops a joint from breaking through a visible surface.
- **Depth** comes from ray casts into both parts from the centre and 8 rim points. Pins get shorter (down to 4 mm per side), or move elsewhere.
- Joints are spread by farthest-point sampling: at least 2 per patch so parts cannot rotate, and 3–4 on large faces.

- **Your joint style wins.** The chosen point joint is placed wherever at least two fit, even on thin shells (in thicker spots such as rims). If only one fits, you get that one plus a warning, because a single pin lets the parts rotate; one click switches that contact to a seam or a keyed peg.

- **Substitutions are never silent.** Only when the chosen style cannot be placed at all does a contact get a seam picked by wall thickness: tongue and groove if the wall is ≥ 3 × the minimum wall, half lap if ≥ 2 ×, else finger joint (dovetails only when you choose them). Each one shows a badge such as "Dowels → lap seam: wall 2.3 mm" in the plan summary and on the joint map, with the exact reaso

- Changing the **Joints** selector re-places the automatic joints on the current cuts at once; cuts and manual joints are kept. The last settings are restored from browser storage (the page says so); **Reset to defaults** goes back to Dowel pins (glue).
- Integrated pegs and seams go on the part that does **not** print on that face, so the face stays flat on the bed. Horizontal holes get teardrop roofs, and horizontal pegs get a flat underside.

Clearances are radial, per side, and editable. The defaults for a 0.4 mm nozzle are: press 0.05, glue 0.15, slip 0.20, snap 0.25, seam 0.15 mm. A 0.6 mm nozzle adds 0.05 mm.

- **Physical fit is untested until you print the coupon.** The clearances are geometric. Your printer, filament and slicer decide the real fit. Step 5 generates a **joint test coupon** with six graded clearances. Print it first, then enter the loosest step that still holds.

- A 40 × 40 support raster for each signed orientation: downward faces steeper than 45°, weighted by face area and height above the bed. It clips original triangles to the BSP cell, includes cut caps with holes, unions overlapping columns, and excludes bed contact within 0.6 mm.

- Both cut ranking and print-orientation selection use the proxy. Fit is a separate gate. Required fit cuts precede optional support cuts; a fitting piece can now be split when savings outweigh the extra part/seam cost.
- Bounded candidate search: up to five offset bands per normal, at most 30 shortlisted cuts. Representative hulls rank orientations, then exact hulls confirm feasibility.

- **Fewer parts ↔ Less support** slider, Balanced default `0.5`. Zero retains the original parts-first objective; the far-right endpoint still charges for additional parts. The API clamps the weight, and the CLI supports `-support-weight`.
- Per-part `supportVolume` in mm³; UI aggregate in cm³, explicitly labelled a **proxy**. Consecutive auto plans show the previous part count/proxy when the other settings are unchanged.

The default's proxy penalty is 100 score units per 100 cm³ saved, versus 100 per extra estimated part, before seam penalties. The weight enters quadratically. This calibration is inspectable in `supportCost`, not trained on invented material data.
